## Empty subset2 joins its `]]`

Nothing stands between the `[[` and the `]]`, so the join has to happen on the
bump of the `[[` itself.

```r
x[[]]
```

```cst

    bom_token: missing (optional),
    statements: RStatementList [
        RExpressionStatement {
            expression: RSubset2 {
                function: RIdentifier {

                arguments: RSubset2Arguments {
                    l_brack2_token: L_BRACK2@1..3 "[[" [] [],
                    items: RArgumentList [],
                    r_brack2_token: R_BRACK2@3..5 "]]" [] [],
                },
            },
            semicolon_token: missing (optional),
        },
    ],
```

## Lookahead for `=` survives the `]]` join

Looking one token past an argument name buffers whatever follows it, which for
`x[[a]]` is the very `]` the next bump has to re-lex into `]]`.

```r
x[[a = 1]]
x[[a = x[[b = 1]]]]
```

## Subset2 arguments

```r
fn
fn[[a]]
fn[[a, b]]
fn[[...]]
fn[[a, ..., b]]

fn[[a = 1]]
fn[[a = ]]

fn[[a = 1, b = 2]]
fn[[a = , b = 2]]

fn[[... = 1]]
fn[[... =]]

fn[["arg" = 1]]
fn[["arg" =]]

# Comma tests
fn[[,]]
fn[[,,,]]
fn[[,,a,,b,,]]

# Comment tests
fn[[
  # comment
]]
fn[[,
  # comment
,]]
fn[[
  a, # comment1
  b # comment2
]]
fn[[
  a # comment1
  = # comment2

{expr}[[a = 1]]
```
